text:
jamie: seeing big spike in tail latency and 5xx from eu-west1 -> edge caches. cloud interconnect QoS alerts firing. also noticing GPU pools in eu-west1 reporting failed healthchecks and being drained. anyone oncall?

ana: same here, dashboards show packet loss ~10-20% on the interconnect. pods failing init with connection resets to origin. example log line: `healthcheck failed: connection reset by peer`

mike: checked LB backends — healthy backend count dropping fast. autoscaler tried to provision but new nodes fail init with curl 503 to /health. local probe: ```curl -v http://127.0.0.1:8080/health \n* Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 8080 (#0)\n> GET /health HTTP/1.1\n> Host: localhost\n> \n< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable\n< content-type: application/json\n```

lina: starting routing mitigation now — changing global LB weights: send 80% traffic to eu-central, keep 20% to eu-west1-d reserved pool. enabling edge-cache-fallback header so clients can hit stale cache for a short window. applying canary first.

deploy-bot: Canary routing update applied: weights=eu-central:80,eu-west1-d:20, cache-fallback=on :white_check_mark:

ana: we need to avoid overloading eu-central reserved pool. plan: scale reserved pool there (will take ~12-15m), enable preemptible fallback for non-prod and batch jobs, and reduce batch_size for interactive classes from 64 -> 32 to keep latency under SLOs.

jamie: also going to disable KV-cache invalidation cluster-wide temporarily to reduce write amplification and speed startups, and reduce batch window to 25ms. patching config now: ```kubectl -n runtime patch cm inference-config --patch '{"data":{"kv_cache_invalidate":"false","batch_window":"25ms"}}'```

mike: patch applied, nodes reloaded. pod startup times improved, fewer 503s on init. still seeing some 502s coming from edge-cache origin timeouts — bumping origin timeout from 1.2s -> 3s as temporary stopgap.

ana: opened ticket with cloud provider (INC-987654) — provider acknowledged QoS shaping on interconnect due to upstream maintenance, ETA ~2h and they've escalated to interconnect ops. attaching packet captures and BGP flaps.

lina: cost note: spinning additional on-demand GPUs in eu-central ~ $X/hr, tracking under INF-2026-332. recommend we keep dedicated/reserved for prod-critical only and move non-prod or low-priority batch to preemptible pools until this stabilizes.

jamie: :rotating_light: post-incident actions: add region healthscore to routing policies so we auto-shift traffic by health*latency, and add an interconnect synthetic probe that runs a real inference probe every minute (exercise path: client->edge->interconnect->origin). also include automatic burst capacity policy to bring up cross-region nodes.

mike: will update runbook and add a checklist for 'interconnect QoS degradation' with commands we used, escalation contacts, and the gcloud commands for spinning emergency nodes. prepping PR for runbook now.

ana: monitoring shows recovery in progress. last check 1817654399: eu-west1 backend healthy count up to 99%, packet loss back to baseline. cloud provider marking incident resolved on their side.

sre-bot: Incident 1817654321 marked resolved by ana at 1817654399. Follow-up ticket INF-2026-332 created for postmortem and cost reconciliation. :white_check_mark:
